message:
## Verdict: about 8.4 out of 10. This is a top-tier entry.

You read the brief correctly. The thing that separates this from a typical entry is that the music's structure comes from the recursion itself: each call is a note, each base case is a bell, and each return resolves a phrase. Most entries will just turn Fibonacci numbers into pitches, and judges from a data-structures background will see the difference immediately. Wander vs Bloom (depth-first vs breadth-first) and "step inside any branch" are the two strongest ideas in the build.

### What I checked
- **`npm run verify`** passes: typecheck, lint, unit tests and build.
- **End-to-end tests:** all 8 pass on Chromium, at desktop and phone sizes. That covers smoke, keyboard, step-inside, accessibility checks and export. The exported WAV was 8.5 MB at an average level (RMS) of −16.1 dBFS, which is inside your target range.
- **The app itself:** I ran the built app and took screenshots at 1440×900 and 390×844 at 0, 8 and 28 seconds. There were no console errors, only one Tone.js timing warning.
- **I could not check:** the live links (GitHub Pages and the Vercel mirror) are blocked from this container, and I can't hear audio. Open both links yourself on a phone.

### Score by criterion
| Criterion | Weight | Score | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Relaxation & UX | 35% | 8.5 | The landing screen is calm and the Begin step works. Moods, ambience, breathing, sleep timer and zen mode are all there. Three issues are listed below. |
| Musical quality | 25% | 7.5 (by evidence, not by ear) | Notes are locked to the scale, chords are voice-led, there are cadences and a proper mix chain. The ceiling is the synthesized sounds, so your own ears decide this one. |
| Creative recursion | 15% | 9.5 | The call tree really is the musical form. The lens, the live call stack, step-inside and two different recursive worlds all show it. |
| Visual design | 10% | 8 | Coherent and good-looking, but the first frame often looks lopsided. |
| Interaction | 10% | 8.5 | Clear labels, shortcuts, share links, a saved garden. |
| Technical | 5% | 9 | Pure tested core, one instrument rack for live and export, CI, audio QA. |

All six mandatory deliverables are met.

### Fix these before 18:30, in priority order
1. **The prompt log link is broken. This is a disqualification risk.** `ai-logs/INDEX.md` and `ai-logs/README.md` point to `PROMPT_LOG.md`, but that file was never committed. The `sessions/*.md` files do contain the prompts, but a judge who clicks the link finds nothing. Also, the index was generated at 08:32 UTC and the last commit was at 09:07 UTC, so recent prompts may be missing. At the very end, run `npm run logs:collect`, commit everything in `ai-logs/` (this judging session included), and check that every link resolves on GitHub.
2. **The first load uses a random seed, and the tree can look lopsided.** I got `sleepy-glade-69`. In Wander mode, at 8 s there was only a single bent stroke, and at 28 s half the tree was grown with the right side of the screen empty. Make the first visit always use a curated, balanced seed such as `still-lake-07` (`src/state/store.ts:152`), and keep random seeds for "New seed". This is a one-line change that protects the 35% criterion.
3. **The playback bar has an overlap at 390 px.** The circular download button sits on top of the `0:27 / 2:47` time label and the right end of the timeline. The mood chips are also cut off at "Deep Ocea" without a fade to show that they scroll.
4. **A Tone.js warning fires on every play:** "Events scheduled inside of scheduled callbacks should use the passed in scheduling time". It comes from something in the scheduled ambience or note callbacks in `src/audio/rack.ts` that doesn't use the `time` it is given. It's only a warning, but it's the one line a judge with DevTools open will see. It may also cause slight timing jitter.
5. **The README mixes two units for loudness.** It gives targets in LUFS but reports measurements as RMS dBFS. Either measure LUFS properly, or say "RMS ≈ −16 dBFS" and stop there.

### What to listen for (you're the ears)
- **Each mood:** within the first 2 minutes, is there any harsh pluck or high bell?
- **Switching moods mid-song:** is there any click?
- **Deep Ocean (Lydian):** do the semitone passing notes ever sound sour?
- **The ending:** does the piece really land on the home chord?

Nothing in the repo was changed. My screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-seedsong/7de382cf-83bc-5897-b5f5-a5665b7c642b/scratchpad/`.

Its music is a separate recording at 76 BPM (`demo/trailer.json`, `demo/trailer-music.mjs`). The 2:47 in the playback bar is one full song for the default tree (255 branches, about 60 BPM). Turning Depth down makes the song shorter.

**What changed:**
1. **Phone playback bar:** the download button no longer sits on top of the time label. It's fixed at 390 px and 320 px. On desktop, the zoom icon no longer overlaps the end of the timeline either.
2. **Mood chips on phones:** the right edge of the row now fades out, so it's clear you can swipe for more.
3. **Tone.js warning:** I traced it to Tone itself, not your code. When the pad creates a new voice, Tone stops some oscillators without passing a time, which triggers the warning. Nothing plays at the wrong time. I filter out only that one message; every other Tone warning still shows. The console is now clean.
4. **"Lopsided tree":** I was wrong about the cause in my review. I scored 400 seeds and every full tree is balanced. The empty half comes from Wander's depth-first order, which finishes the left side before starting the right. Instead of a curated seed, the tree to come is now drawn as a faint silhouette that fades in after the first couple of seconds. Wander no longer leaves half the sky empty, and you can see the whole call tree waiting to run.
5. **README:** the loudness line now says the numbers are RMS, not LUFS. The unit-test count is corrected from 24 to 30.

`npm run verify` passes (30 unit tests). All 8 end-to-end tests pass on desktop and phone, including the WAV export at −17.3 dBFS RMS. Screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-seedsong/7de382cf-83bc-5897-b5f5-a5665b7c642b/scratchpad/` (the `v2-*` files).

Your two Windows sessions dropped out of the table, because their transcripts only exist on your PC. I left that file uncommitted. When I tried to restore the old index and add this session as row 3 by hand, the permission system blocked it as an edit to the AI logs. Two ways to fix it:
- **Easier:** after you pull this branch on your Windows machine, run `npm run logs:collect` there. It sees all three sessions and rebuilds the index properly.
